name: Supporting Teachers of English Learners
title: Supporting Teachers of English Learners
answer: Most English learners are taught by teachers who are not language specialists, so AI can help those teachers draft supports like sentence frames, glossaries, and simplified texts. The English language development specialist reviews and improves these materials, and districts should protect specialists' time for coaching and direct work with students rather than only material production.

sections.body: English learners spend most of their day with general education teachers who have no language specialization, and those teachers need practical support they can act on. AI offers part of that support by helping a teacher draft sentence frames, glossaries, and simplified texts for a unit. The English language development specialist then reviews what the AI produced, so the materials reflect real language expertise. Over time this work builds a reusable library of supports instead of one-off handouts. The idea solves the gap between the specialist knowledge a classroom needs and the specialist time a school actually has.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, a science teacher preparing a unit can use AI to draft sentence frames, a glossary, and a simplified version of the text, then send those drafts to the English language development specialist for review. The specialist's corrections and additions become part of a growing library the teacher can reuse in later units. Professional learning supports this by showing teachers how to prompt for a text at a particular level, how to check a translation, and why AI feedback on learners' writing still needs a person to review it. Teachers who understand the limits of these tools use them more wisely, and the text points to Chapter 20 for a fuller treatment of professional learning. The text does not give separate grade band guidance for this idea.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or formal evidence label for this idea. It describes what teachers and specialists can do and how professional learning should be run, but it does not report research findings. This idea therefore rests on practice and on the judgment of the specialists who review the materials rather than on research cited in the text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The expertise of English language development specialists is what makes the materials good, and the text states plainly that it cannot be replaced. AI feedback on learners' writing needs review, and translations need checking, so a person stays responsible for what reaches students. Specialists are often stretched thin across many schools, and districts should protect their time for coaching teachers and working with students, not just for producing materials. The decisions about what a learner needs and whether a support is appropriate remain with the teacher and the specialist.
